mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consistent decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations adjust downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of periods with declining GDP, or the correlation between GDP declines and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a surge in supply-side activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production boosts corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is above 4% and the CPI is increasing by more than 0.3% per month, the combination signals an inflationary environment with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary period with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction effect between high FEDFUNDS and rising CPIAUCSL on negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls and a decrease in the unemployment rate within a month signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction effect between PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases on positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts by more than 5% in a month signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the broader economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between HOUST declines and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in real personal consumption expenditures over two consecutive months signals a strengthening demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of periods with increasing RSAFS, or the correlation between RSAFS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
